rawFindings.title: Fixer now edits the wrong range for constructor string patterns
rawFindings.explanation: For `new RegExp('bar    ')`, `valueStart` points to the opening quote, but `regexResults.index` is relative to the extracted string value. The fixer range currently starts at `valueStart + regexResults.index`, which includes the quote offset only once and happens to work for the first match, but the new `count` calculation changes the reported span to just the space run while still using the string literal node range. When the match occurs at the end of a string literal, replacing only `[valueSt
rawFindings.suggestion: Compute the replacement range from the literal contents only and preserve the surrounding quotes, e.g. use `node.arguments[0].range`/`token.range` offsets explicitly for string literals and verify the start/end positions against the literal text before replacing.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: `new RegExp('bar    ')` is autofixed using a range that does not reliably cover only the spaces inside the string literal, producing incorrect rewritten source in edge cases.

rawFindings.title: The new regex skips spaces after an escaped quantifier opener
rawFindings.explanation: The updated pattern only recognizes a run of spaces when it is followed by `+`, `*`, `{`, `?`, another non-quantifier character, or end-of-string. This narrows detection compared with the previous implementation and fails to report patterns where the run precedes other regex punctuation that is still part of the same tokenization, such as spaces before `)` inside a grouped subpattern. A concrete example is `/a(  )b/`, which contains multiple spaces in the regex source but is no longer matched by
rawFindings.suggestion: Use a token-based scan that looks for any run of two or more spaces in the regex source rather than constraining the following character, or explicitly enumerate all valid continuations the rule should handle.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: `/a(  )b/` is no longer reported even though it contains multiple spaces in the regex source.
